approach: The scene's job is to get the Mac Studio back onto SJ's desk so the police find it there, and almost all of its time goes on a malware chat that s22 repeats nearly word for word. The cuts below strip it in order of least loss; taking all of them leaves a wordless return (Brendan carries the machine in, puts it down, SJ chuckles), the first news chyron, a two-line goodbye, and SJ plugging the machine in. That is effectively cutting the scene while keeping the return as a visible beat.

suggestions.title: Cut the hackernews malware conversation
suggestions.why: s22_front_door already has SJ say the same thing to Marcus, almost verbatim: 'A long-lived key... It didn't break anything. It was allowed to do everything it did. That's my memo.' Playing it here first blunts that line, which lands harder when SJ meets it fresh in s22. s20_l18 has already paid off the memo through Brendan. s20b_l23 is an internal-state direction the back row cannot see.
suggestions.keeps: The JWT memo thread survives in s20_l18 and s22_front_door. The Kazakhstan chyron (s20b_l24) is not in this cut and can still run behind the return. s20b_l51 ('reads more of the comments') still reads as SJ browsing on screen. Lost: Brendan's guilty '...Mm.' and the dramatic irony of SJ admiring the attack in front of the machine.

against.s20b_l20: Everyone's speculating about it, but when folks compare notes none of it lines up, so maybe it's just a group launching a bunch of different attacks.
against.s20b_l21: Somebody wiped a whole cluster and rebuilt it from backup, and it came back inside the hour. They think the backups were already carrying it.
against.s20b_l22: That does sound interesting... I wonder if that's related to the Ukraine or Iran war...
against.s20b_l25: Do you know what's actually clever about it, though? It seems to be using Long lived API keys to spread among other things.. you know, the thing I wrote about in my JWT memo?
against.s20b_l26: It didn't break anything to get in, that's the thing. Every single thing it did, it was allowed to do.
against.s20b_l29: I'd love to see the logs, it's a bummer I can't help do incident response..

suggestions.riskWhy: No plot is lost: the attack's method lands in s22_front_door, which this cut lets SJ say fresh, and it also removes a small continuity snag where SJ already knows about the keys yet asks Marcus 'How did it get in?' (s22_how). What goes is the dramatic irony of SJ admiring the attack in front of the machine while Brendan sits silent.
loses: Character: SJ admiring the malware's design and wishing he could see the logs, with the Mac Studio that did it on the table
Character: Brendan's guilty '...Mm.' and breath out (s20b_l27, s20b_l28), his only reaction to the news in SJ's presence
Colour: the wiped cluster that came back from backup inside the hour (nowhere else)
Plot: SJ linking the attack to his JWT memo (also in s22_front_door and s20_l18)
Setup: s20b_l51 'reads more of the comments' loses its referent; it needs 'more of' dropped or it reads oddly

suggestions.title: Cut SJ telling Brendan he emailed a friend
suggestions.why: SJ's care for Brendan after the layoffs is already on stage in s19 (the resume advice, s19_l37 to s19_l39) and in the 06:02 text he sends in s20_l68. This is a third instance of the same kindness.
suggestions.keeps: SJ's motive for taking the fall is still spelled out by the narrator in s23b ('Eighteen months costs him less than it would cost Brendan'). Lost: SJ's 'best engineer I've worked with in ten years', which mirrors Marcus calling SJ 'the best engineer I've ever worked with' in s23_l32, and the 'Especially if it's a no' line, which is very SJ. The author should decide whether that mirror is worth keeping.

against.s20b_l33: Oh, I emailed my friend about you.
against.s20b_l35: I said you're the best engineer I've worked with in ten years and she should talk to you before somebody else does.
against.s20b_l36: Oh SJ... you didn't have to do that.
against.s20b_l37: I know. Let me know if she comes back to you. Even if it's a no. Especially if it's a no, actually, because then I'll call her.

suggestions.riskWhy: Loses SJ's one direct praise of Brendan and a very SJ line, but no plot: his care for Brendan after the layoffs is already shown in s19_l37 to s19_l39 and s20_l68, and his motive for taking the fall is stated in s23b.
loses: Character: SJ calling Brendan 'the best engineer I've worked with in ten years', the only time SJ praises Brendan; it reverses the motif of others calling SJ the best (s01b_l3, s07_l12, s14a_l43, s23_l32)
Joke: 'Especially if it's a no, actually, because then I'll call her.'
Character: SJ going out of his way for Brendan just after Brendan has unknowingly framed him, which sharpens Brendan's guilt

suggestions.title: Cut the drink offer and SJ's eleven resumes
suggestions.why: SJ's 'just get them out' advice is already given in s19_l37 to s19_l39 and repeated in his text in s20_l68 ('send out three job applications before lunch'). s20b_l12 is internal state that cannot be staged.
suggestions.keeps: The layoff advice thread is intact in s19 and s20. Lost: the small, sad detail of two automated rejections on the same day.

against.s20b_l10: Do you want a drink? I've got... coffee... tea...?

against.s20b_l15: It's what I told you. Just get them out.

suggestions.riskWhy: Repetition: the 'just get them out' advice is already given in s19_l37 to s19_l39 and s20_l68, and s20b_l12 is internal state the back row cannot see. Only a small sad detail of colour goes.
loses: Colour: eleven resumes and two automated rejections on the same day (nowhere else)
Character: the only glimpse of SJ's own job hunt after the layoff, and his forced 'keeping the momentum up'
Nothing substantive in s20b_l10, s20b_l11, s20b_l12: drink offer and an internal-state direction

suggestions.title: Cut the unlocked-model exchange
suggestions.why: The narrator has already told the audience in s20_l37 that SJ went out of his way to find an unlocked Qwen because of the refusals, and s22_unlocked and s22_which bring it back. Nothing later depends on Brendan hearing it from SJ.
suggestions.keeps: The unlocked-model thread lives in s20_l37, s20_l43 and s22. Lost: Brendan's half-truth 'a cyber security audit', a small bit of irony.

against.s20b_l6: What did you use it for?

against.s20b_l8: Oh yeah, I don't know if I told you that part, I got tired of the refusals so I found an unlocked model

suggestions.riskWhy: The fact that SJ chose an unlocked model is already told in s20_l37 and brought back in s20_l43 and s22_unlocked, so this repeats it. What goes is Brendan's half-truth and a small bit of irony.
loses: Plot: SJ deliberately found an unlocked model because of the refusals (also in s20_l37)
Character: Brendan's half-truth 'a cyber security audit', the closest he comes to confessing
Joke: SJ's offhand 'I don't know if I told you that part', delivered to the man it doomed

suggestions.title: Cut the jacket and hangover exit
suggestions.why: A stalled exit beat. Brendan's guilt is better carried by him leaving quickly than by a hangover excuse, and the drinking was already established in s19 and s20_l1.
suggestions.keeps: Brendan's exit survives in s20b_l45 to s20b_l47 ('Thanks, SJ.' 'Any time.'). Lost: the jacket taking 'slightly longer than it needs to' and SJ's 'Go home. Eat something.'

against.s20b_l41: Yeah. Maybe still hung over a bit from last night.

suggestions.riskWhy: Raised from low: the slow jacket and the hangover excuse are Brendan's last visible guilt in front of SJ, and a second small lie to his face. This is a unique character and staging beat, not padding.
loses: Character: Brendan covering with 'still hung over a bit'
Character: SJ's 'Go home. Eat something.'

suggestions.title: Make the return wordless
suggestions.why: With the rest of the scene cut, the return reads from the back row on its own: Brendan carries the Mac Studio in and puts it down (s20b_l2, s20b_l5), and SJ plugs it in once he has gone (s20b_l48 to s20b_l50). s20_l72 has already given Brendan's reason for bringing it back. If the scene is cut entirely instead, the return needs one stage direction at the top of s22, for example: 'BRENDAN sets the Mac Studio down on SJ's desk, nods, and goes.'
suggestions.keeps: The machine is visibly back at SJ's, which s22_studio, s22_l72 and the prosecutor's 'recovered from the defendant's home' (s23_l10) depend on. Lost: Brendan's 'slow token rate' excuse, which is a quiet joke.

against.s20b_l3: You really don't have to give it back so soon, you barely got to play with it...
against.s20b_l4: That's okay, it turns out I don't have the patience for the slow token rate after all...

suggestions.riskWhy: The return still reads visually (s20b_l2, s20b_l5, s20b_l48 to s20b_l50) and s20_l72 gives Brendan's reason, so no plot goes. It loses a quiet joke, and s20b_l5 'SJ chuckles' needs trimming because the line he chuckles at is gone.
loses: Joke: Brendan's 'slow token rate' excuse
Character: SJ's 'you barely got to play with it', his generosity in lending the machine
Character: Brendan returning the machine under a cover story rather than confessing (motive still given in s20_l72)
Staging: s20b_l5 'SJ chuckles' is orphaned unless edited

ifDeleted.summary: Brendan returns the Mac Studio and mentions the security audit. SJ, delighted, tells him about the unlocked model, reads him the first hackernews reports of the worm and says he has recommended him to a friend. Nobody realises what is sitting on the table. Most of the plot is repeated in s22 (the key, the memo, the unlocked model, the 'allowed to do' line). Deleting the scene loses Brendan's last appearance on stage and the warm dramatic irony that makes SJ's later plea for Brendan's sake land harder. One narrator bridge covers the handback.

changes.detail: Narrator bridge covering the handback and the clue SJ needs later.
changes.text: NARRATOR: That afternoon he gives the Mac Studio back. He tells SJ he ran a security audit on it. SJ tells him the model was unlocked. Neither of them thinks about it again.

changes.detail: Optional: move the Kazakhstan chyron to directly after the new bridge line so the ticker starts before s22. Otherwise cut it.
Delete the rest of the scene. There is no montage cue to keep.

ifDeleted.riskWhy: The plot survives in s20 and s22, but this is Brendan's farewell and the last warm moment between him and SJ, and SJ's sacrifice in s23b leans on it.
